## 1. Safety rules (all devices, never skip)

Titles only; full text in [AGENT-RULES.md](https://github.com/70b185/Aggregat/blob/master/hardware/AGENT-RULES.md).

- **A1** Do not touch the bootstrap/bootloader or the updater section. [doc]
- **A2** Know the recovery path before anything is flashed. [doc]
- **A3** Back up first. [doc]
- **A4** Never power off during an upgrade. [doc]
- **A5** BOOTSTRAP UPGRADE is the only irreversible step [doc]
- **A6** Verify every candidate image before it is written [doc] [hw]
- **A7** First run of a new DSP/audio build: volume down. [doc]
- **A8** Gate what you ship. [doc]
- **A9** Respect transfer limits. [doc]
- **A10** Mods can be mutually exclusive by OS version. [doc]
- **A11** Rehearse recovery with a stock file before the first modified flash [hw]
- **A12** One change per flash. [doc]
- **A13** Gate DSP code against hardware rules the emulators cannot see. [doc]
- **A14** Check the size margin at every loader stage, not just the file size. [hw]
- **A15** Leave the panel-MCU blob, its updater and section 8 (Outbox 8 firmware) stock [doc]
- **A16** Withdraw builds that lose sound. [hw]
- **A17** In the startup menu never press TRIG 2 or TRIG 3 by habit [doc]
- **A18** "Not hardware-tested" must travel with the file. [doc]
- **A19** Red-team your own safety gate. [doc]
- **A20** The progress bar is not proof. [doc]
- **A21** Upload over USB without auto-commit, then commit explicitly. [hw]
- **A22** Never touch an FPGA bitstream or its configuration path [doc]
- **A23** "Success! Rebooting" is not proof. [doc] [hw]
- **A24** Keep private card data above the MmcFs guard and above `0x800000`; [doc]
- **A25** Guard each block, not the average (DT2/DN2 SHARC). [hw]
- **A26** On DT2, publish to reply words 670-676 only. [hw]
- **A27** Analog Heat +FX: change only section 3 (MAIN OS), and keep custom code below `0x40206000`. [hw]
- **A28** Code you copy into SHARC memory at run time must be written back from the data cache before it runs. [hw]
- **A29** Leave a trail the ColdFire can read when the DSP stops. [hw]
- **A30** Keep the container under `0x200000` bytes and section 2's table version stock. [doc]
- **A31** A negative is only as good as the search that produced it. [doc]
- **A32** Store each section the way the original stores it. [doc]
- **A33** Never store a DAG register through its own DAG, and keep SIMD data moves where stock has them. [hw]
- **A34** On ColdFire-audio devices (Syntakt, Digitakt mk1, Digitone mk1), the audio interrupt is the budget. [hw]
- **A35** Budget SHARC code with silicon costs, not instruction counts. [hw]
- **A36** The startup-menu recovery listens to DIN MIDI only, on every Elektron box documented here. [hw]
- **A37** A busy share is not headroom (DT2/DN2 SHARC). [hw]
- **A38** If the OS carries a copy of the bootstrap, no patch may touch that copy or the check that triggers it (A4 MK1, Rytm MK1, Machinedrum). [doc]
- **A39** Never let a USB control transfer (EP0) data stage be a whole multiple of 64 bytes on the ColdFire USB controller with stock's driver. [hw]
- **A40** Qualify any startup change after a long power-off, not only after quick restarts or in the emulator. [hw]
- **A41** Disassemble what you assemble. [doc] [emu] [hw]
- **A42** ColdFire is not a full 68000: check every addressing-mode combination against the ColdFire manual, not against the emulator. [emu] [hw]
- **A43** A cave is free only after it survived a hard run on the unit. [hw]
- **A44** A load governor acts on sustained load, never on one block that is already over. [hw]
- **A45** Keep the end of every SHARC hardware loop in 48-bit ISA (DT2/DN2). [hw]
- **A46** Keep a decoded section 7 under `0xfffff` bytes, and count the decoded size, not the stored one (DT2/DN2). [hw]
- **A47** Before a stock storage command, check the card is idle; never assume the stock driver times out (DN2, likely DT2). [hw]
- **A48** Find out what is cached from the OS's own start-up, not the bootstrap; keep hot-path accesses to uncached memory few and word-sized. [hw]
- **A49** Test the first install on a unit in stock condition, not only on the developer's unit. [hw]
- **A50** Go through stock's own input paths; never post into its internal queues or overwrite state another core reads. [hw]
- **A51** Run a long soak before a release, and mask every counter to its register width. [hw]
- **A52** Keep per-sample DSP accesses out of external DDR (DT2/DN2). [hw]
- **A53** Use only addresses the unit decodes after the OS has set up its memory map. [hw]
- **A54** Unload a module only while nothing uses it, and give the loader a way out of its own recovery state. [hw]
- **A55** Do not switch the USB mode at run time in anything you ship until it has passed a long switch loop on a unit; prefer asking the user to set the mode in the menu. [hw]
- **A56** On the Octatrack, ColdFire time added to the frame interrupt can cause or cure a DSP stall by a few microseconds either way, so an A/B that only adds or removes a module is not evidence about that module. [hw]
- **A57** On the Octatrack, do card I/O only where stock does its own (its card task), or load the data into RAM first; never read the card from the UI tick or a frame hook. [hw]
- **A58** A DSP test passes only when sound comes out, and check the analog outputs through a loopback, not only a USB recording. [hw]
- **A59** Check a firmware value against the audio output before you gate sound on it, and test in the mode the user plays. [hw]
- **A60** Every byte a mod stores in a stock record must pass stock's own check with the mod absent. [hw]
- **A61** Code hooked into the stock USB init must be safe in interrupt context and give the same result on every run (DT2/DN2). [doc]
- **A62** When you call a stock routine at a site other mods hook, set every register stock's own caller sets, not only the C arguments. [hw]
- **A63** When a USB interface's host-side setup can go stale on Windows, change `bcdDevice` with the release that needs it. [hw]
- **A64** When you hand the OS a structure, find out whether it copies it before use; later changes must go to the copy it reads. [hw]
- **A65** Judge a load budget by the playing load and include the new module's own cost. [hw]
- **A66** On a DSP that waits on a second core, put long work at the end of the frame, not at its head. [hw]
- **A67** Never raise a note's trig and its end in the same audio block. [hw]
- **A68** Before a software reset, anything the next boot must read has to be in RAM, not only in the cache. [hw]
- **A69** Take the stock bytes a run-time patch replays from a copy made before the OS and the flashed build ran, never from live RAM. [emu]
- **A70** Never land a change on the tick a stock event is due and rely on a tie between its time and the clock. [hw]
- **A71** Write at most one value per track, step and parameter in one change. [emu]
- **A72** When you extend a stock table that a setting indexes, extend every table that setting indexes, including tables the OS builds in RAM at run time. [hw]
- **A73** A neutral setting of an effect must give back stock's routing, not only a flat response. [hw]
- **A74** Build mod code with undefined-behaviour warnings as errors, at least `-Werror=return-type`. [emu]
- **A75** On the Model:Cycles, an added machine whose oscillator runs on through a trig must keep the stock VCA from cutting at the trig. [hw]
- **A76** Syntakt: never write SPI NOR `0x300000-0x380000`, and keep the OS container under 2 MB. [doc]
- **A77** Before you store mod data in a byte of a stock record, find every stock routine that reads or writes it, and test with a project that uses every feature of that record. [hw]
- **A78** When a base keeps its own data inside a stock record, shrink the core's area by the same bytes and refuse an overlap at build time. [hw]

## 4. Bugs in Elektron's own OS (check before you blame your mod)

- **SB15** A random exception while browsing (filesystem block cache) (Model:Cycles, OS 1.13; open in stock; fixed by a mod). Workaround: fixed by Model-TG ("a long-standing stock bug"), and in builds that include it (Modded-Cycles lists it).

## 5. What went wrong on real units

- **I88** Turned knobs did not reach the sample being previewed. Cause: the OS copies the browser's sound into its own preview buffer (two take turns), and preview notes read that copy, not the sound the mod handed out. Fix: One-Shot 0.17 writes the track's knobs (not the key) into the buffer that holds the copy on each tick. Rules: A64.
- **I113** A previewed sample played to its end however short the key press (Model:Cycles). Cause: the mod sent the note-off at once; the OS chained it with the note into one batch, and the amp envelope ignores an end that comes in the trig's own block, so with GATE on the note stayed in hold. The project's notes had claimed the preview no longer held, without a check. Fix: One-Shot 0.18 / model27 0.66 records the note and raises the voice's end flag (+0x3c) in the first block without a trig, and hooks both releases (pad `0x4001d0fc`, TRIG keys `0x40019c84`); flashed from the live page 2026-11-15: taps stay short, held keys sound until let go. Rules: A67,A31.
- **I125** A bit-exact sub oscillator sounded as buzz and crackle on the unit (model27 MAXSAW, Model:Cycles). Cause: the device did what the design said: Sub shifted the centre's naive sawtooth two octaves down, which brings as many overtones as fundamental (its reset every 15 ms a buzz), and the pitch-tracked high-pass moved down with it and let 4-8 dB more aliasing through. Recordings matched the host core within 0.6 dB in third-octave bands, so every proof (interpreter, Unicorn bit-exact) had passed. Fix: a listening page of seven sub variants; the maintainer chose an extra naive sawtooth two octaves down through a 2-pole low-pass at the note, added after the high-pass (MAXSAW 0.2); on the unit "sub klingt jetzt gut" (the sub sounds good now). Released in 0.69, flashed from the page with every card. Rules: A58.
- **I140** A 70 % CPU budget greyed out every heavier machine on old projects (Modded Cycles Techno Edition). Cause: the project keeps the six stock machines, which with the rest of the OS already count about 74 % against the CPU Lim default of 70 %. Fix: v1.4.1 sets the default to 80 % (a user who had chosen 80 % now reads 70 % and must step it on). New projects start with EMPTY on all six tracks. Rules: A65.
- **I144** An added machine clicked at trigs through the stock VCA (model27 TERRA, Model:Cycles). Cause: the stock VCA (`0x400a9430`) cuts the level in a trig's block and jumps at the attack. TONE's chain does that to TERRA's output, which runs on through the trig without a reset. Fix: TERRA 0.2 clears voice `+0x34` and `+0x38` only for the VCA call and restores them before PUNCH; the VCA ramps from its last level each block. Unicorn retrig check at DECAY 127/60/30: gain never dips toward zero, largest step a frame 0.0014/0.0064/0.0190. Rules: A75.

## 7. Open tests and tasks you could settle

- **H42** (stock) On a Model:Cycles with stock OS 1.13, a project track holding an out-of-range machine number plays CHORD with wrong settings, shows *Error* on MACHINES, and is repaired by turning LEVEL/DATA, without any crash. Test: Save a project with an added machine on a mod, flash stock, open it and play; then turn LEVEL/DATA on MACHINES.
- **H46** (stock) A Model:Cycles OS `.syx` with more than 16,270 packets (packet numbers past 16,383) is refused or fails during the update. Test: Do not flash such a file. Instead count the packets of your build and check that each packet number's two bytes are below 0x80.

Report results with the [test-result issue form](https://github.com/70b185/Aggregat/issues/new?template=test-result.yml).

## 9. All 92 facts, best evidence first

- [hw] CPU: ColdFire MCF54415CMJ250 (chip marking read 2026-09-30): MCF5441x, V4 core with EMAC, 250 MHz, no separate DSP. All audio is ColdFire assembly. It is the same CPU family as Digitakt mk1, Digitone mk1, Rytm and A4; the Octatrack is the exception. The MCF54418 reference manual applies. `[hw]` — `model-cycles-samples#454f0b95` [hardware/devices/model-cycles-samples.md:9](https://github.com/70b185/Aggregat/blob/master/hardware/devices/model-cycles-samples.md#L9) · Model:Cycles and Model:Samples - OS 1.13 / Platform
- [hw] Audio: 6 tracks, rendered per 32-sample block (0.67 ms) in the audio interrupt. The stock OS already takes about 77 % of each block, even when stopped, because all tracks and effects are computed every block. Peaks reach 99 % with heavy added engines. `[hw]` — `model-cycles-samples#f6da9f46` [hardware/devices/model-cycles-samples.md:10](https://github.com/70b185/Aggregat/blob/master/hardware/devices/model-cycles-samples.md#L10) · Model:Cycles and Model:Samples - OS 1.13 / Platform
- [doc] [hw] The startup menu lives in flash that OS updates never write. Hold FUNC at power-on, TRIG 4 = OS UPGRADE, "READY TO RECEIVE". It listens to MIDI IN only, never USB. — `model-cycles-samples#b3624cd5` [hardware/devices/model-cycles-samples.md:15](https://github.com/70b185/Aggregat/blob/master/hardware/devices/model-cycles-samples.md#L15) · Model:Cycles and Model:Samples - OS 1.13 / Recovery
- [doc] [hw] Model:Cycles' MIDI IN is a 3.5 mm TRS jack (type A and B both work). A mono TS cable does not work. Use the supplied DIN adapter if your interface has DIN. — `model-cycles-samples#ddb912c6` [hardware/devices/model-cycles-samples.md:16](https://github.com/70b185/Aggregat/blob/master/hardware/devices/model-cycles-samples.md#L16) · Model:Cycles and Model:Samples - OS 1.13 / Recovery
- [doc] [hw] Takes 5-10 minutes; the unit restarts by itself. — `model-cycles-samples#2bce129e` [hardware/devices/model-cycles-samples.md:17](https://github.com/70b185/Aggregat/blob/master/hardware/devices/model-cycles-samples.md#L17) · Model:Cycles and Model:Samples - OS 1.13 / Recovery
- [hw] If it stays on "RECEIVING..." a packet was lost: power cycle and send slower (Modded Cycles' flasher pace 1.4 by default, 2.0 when it fails). `[hw]` — `model-cycles-samples#26b97ccc` [hardware/devices/model-cycles-samples.md:18](https://github.com/70b185/Aggregat/blob/master/hardware/devices/model-cycles-samples.md#L18) · Model:Cycles and Model:Samples - OS 1.13 / Recovery
- [doc] [hw] Free space is scarce. The project's main source of code room is freed sprite masks: Groups of byte-identical `0xFF` bitmap masks are each referenced by one 32-bit constant. Redirecting that constant to a kept copy renders identically and frees the others. 10 groups, 164 freeable masks, 104-1,024 bytes each. Never write into a kept copy. A registry tool tracks which mod owns which mask. — `model-cycles-samples#1e5faa84` [hardware/devices/model-cycles-samples.md:41](https://github.com/70b185/Aggregat/blob/master/hardware/devices/model-cycles-samples.md#L41) · Model:Cycles and Model:Samples - OS 1.13 / Free space and payloads
- [doc] [hw] Other `0xFF` caves are refused when stock code points into them. — `model-cycles-samples#969e69f4` [hardware/devices/model-cycles-samples.md:45](https://github.com/70b185/Aggregat/blob/master/hardware/devices/model-cycles-samples.md#L45) · Model:Cycles and Model:Samples - OS 1.13 / Free space and payloads
- [emu] [hw] Every stock voice is rendered every block, playing or not: about 7,600 instructions each, so six idle voices cost ~45,800 per block. Stock audio takes ~77 % of the CPU at rest, measured on a unit with a diagnostic load counter (the same figure as in Modded-Cycles' notes). Skipping silent voices cut 77 % of the voice-loop instructions in the emulator; the unit test is still open. `[hw]` / `[emu]` — `model-cycles-samples#a78e5c78` [hardware/devices/model-cycles-samples.md:52](https://github.com/70b185/Aggregat/blob/master/hardware/devices/model-cycles-samples.md#L52) · Model:Cycles and Model:Samples - OS 1.13 / Load and USB lessons from Supermodel / Modded Cycles (AveyCole, OS 1.13; notes 23 and 35, in French)
- [?] [hw] Ported Syntakt engines cost about the same instructions as stock voices (-7 % to +43 %), yet three or more made the unit slow and glitchy. The likely cause is their much larger memory footprint (cache misses), which the emulator does not time. - [hw] Thresholds seen on units: the sound crackles when a block nears 100 % of its time; a single block at 91 % did *not* crackle; the UI was still fluid at ~86 % sustained load and slows above that. `[hw]` — `model-cycles-samples#f8c82655` [hardware/devices/model-cycles-samples.md:63](https://github.com/70b185/Aggregat/blob/master/hardware/devices/model-cycles-samples.md#L63) · Model:Cycles and Model:Samples - OS 1.13 / A load governor that works, and one that didn't (Supermodel notes 30 and 36, Model:Cycles OS 1.13)
- [hw] Mistake 1: reacting to one heavy block. Peaks are isolated: a step where several tracks start (the sequencer takes up to ~7 % of a block), or caches the UI flushed between blocks (+4.6 points). By the time the governor sees such a block, it is already over; cutting a voice can't rescue it and is audible. The fix reacts only to a peak that lasts two blocks, or to sustained load. On a unit: "works well", 6 tracks with effects at 89 % peak / 78 % average, no crackle. `[hw]` — `model-cycles-samples#d97619cf` [hardware/devices/model-cycles-samples.md:69](https://github.com/70b185/Aggregat/blob/master/hardware/devices/model-cycles-samples.md#L69) · Model:Cycles and Model:Samples - OS 1.13 / A load governor that works, and one that didn't (Supermodel notes 30 and 36, Model:Cycles OS 1.13)

Track FX answered CC 75/76 and NRPN 1:22/1:23. `[hw]` — `model-cycles-samples#04affa95` [hardware/devices/model-cycles-samples.md:92](https://github.com/70b185/Aggregat/blob/master/hardware/devices/model-cycles-samples.md#L92) · Model:Cycles and Model:Samples - OS 1.13 / MIDI map, voice internals and SOLID (model27 notes 65, 71-73, OS 1.13, 2026-11-11)

- [emu] [hw] A note and its immediate note-off in one batch leave the note held with GATE on. `0x40092116` chains both into one batch, so one pass of the event loop sets the trig and the end bit; the voice loop `0x400a7d96` writes them as +0x34 (trig) and +0x3c (end), each for that block only; the amp envelope `0x400a9252` sets "released" (+0x244) only when +0x3c is set and +0x34 is clear (`0x400a92ee`), so the end is dropped, and with GATE on (+0x24c) the envelope stays in hold (state 2 at +0x23c). A mod that ends a note must raise the end in a later block than the trig (I113, A67). `[emu]` (envelope run block by block) / `[hw]` (behaviour and fix, 2026-11-15) {model27-chips} — `model-cycles-samples#c1ed872f` [hardware/devices/model-cycles-samples.md:105](https://github.com/70b185/Aggregat/blob/master/hardware/devices/model-cycles-samples.md#L105) · Model:Cycles and Model:Samples - OS 1.13 / Pads, preview notes and the shared sine (model27 notes 60 and 66, MAIN OS 1.13, 2026-11-12)

- [emu] USB multitrack glitches (reported on Reddit after 15-20 minutes): Cause: the OS sends each block to USB right after rendering it, and the 6-channel mod's queue tolerated only 0.2 ms of jitter. With variable engine load (muted tracks, effects off) frames went missing. Fix: send at a fixed time at the start of the next interrupt, align the queue at start-up, and use a 9-slot ring instead of 8. Zero defects in the simulator afterwards. General rule for USB streaming mods: decouple the send time from a variable render time. `[emu]` (cause read in the OS, fix simulated) — `model-cycles-samples#e0c972d2` [hardware/devices/model-cycles-samples.md:56](https://github.com/70b185/Aggregat/blob/master/hardware/devices/model-cycles-samples.md#L56) · Model:Cycles and Model:Samples - OS 1.13 / Load and USB lessons from Supermodel / Modded Cycles (AveyCole, OS 1.13; notes 23 and 35, in French)
- [emu] Mistake 2: an integer moving average that never moves. `slow += (load - slow) >> 8` with load and average in whole percent rounds every step to 0, or to -1 below the average. The "sustained load" rule therefore never fired on a unit. The emulator test hid it because it pre-set the average. Keep fixed-point averages in scaled units (e.g. load << 8), and test them from a cold start. `[emu]` — `model-cycles-samples#a5c5bf10` [hardware/devices/model-cycles-samples.md:73](https://github.com/70b185/Aggregat/blob/master/hardware/devices/model-cycles-samples.md#L73) · Model:Cycles and Model:Samples - OS 1.13 / A load governor that works, and one that didn't (Supermodel notes 30 and 36, Model:Cycles OS 1.13)

- [doc] [emu] CC lookup (Model:Cycles): the CC-to-descriptor table is built at `0x4005a8ce`; CC 16-23 are looked up only in the row of the track's machine, so a shared descriptor on CC 20-23 is never reached, while CC 75-78 reach shared descriptors on all six tracks (`[emu]`, interpreter). CC values are not scaled: the handler `0x4000b568` writes value x 256 and the setter `0x4000b274` clamps to the descriptor's range. - [doc] [emu] Model:Samples running the Cycles OS (notes/57 section 7, from notes/41 section 1): only the running OS checks an update, with its own key. A Cycles OS on a Samples that checks with the Cycles key (installed by hand, or by a tool without the 32-byte key change) refuses the Samples-signed return, and nothing is written. The Samples OS packed in the Model:Cycles container is accepted by such an OS, and the Samples bootstrap boots it (`[emu]`, group 7 of model27's crossflash test). What the unit answers on USB when the key is wrong is not known; model27 assumes an error at the last block. Modded-Cycles, Supermodel and PPPCCC apply the 32-byte change; the Techno Edition supports only the Model:Cycles (read 2026-11-17). `[emu]` / `[doc]` — `model-cycles-samples#facdbbb5` [hardware/devices/model-cycles-samples.md:161](https://github.com/70b185/Aggregat/blob/master/hardware/devices/model-cycles-samples.md#L161) · Model:Cycles and Model:Samples - OS 1.13 / TERRA, far tables and the payload's limits (model27 notes/85 and 57, Model:Cycles OS 1.13, 2026-11-17)

- [doc] Elektron Emu (xerydian): five VST3 plug-ins (Mac, Windows) running each machine's real OS in an emulated CPU - Digitakt II, Syntakt, Analog Rytm MKII, Digitone II, Model:Cycles; the user supplies the `.syx` in a per-machine folder; +Drive emulated and persisted, WAV loading on DT2/Rytm/DN2; Digitone II's DSP is compiled locally on first open (needs a C compiler; otherwise a slow interpreter that renders offline only); limits: Rytm analog voices are a custom model that does not sound like the machine, Syntakt analog tracks 9-12 missing; 2 commits, no licence stated. `[doc]` {elektron-emu} — `toolchain-and-emulators#d1f1bb43` [hardware/common/toolchain-and-emulators.md:81](https://github.com/70b185/Aggregat/blob/master/hardware/common/toolchain-and-emulators.md#L81) · Toolchains and emulators / More emulators and directory snapshots (2026-10-31)
- [doc] EMAC runs with MACSR = `0xa0` (signed fractional), and Unicorn gets it wrong (the same pitfall as Syntakt, Octatrack and DN2). - [doc] Container: ELE3, text header plus section table (16-byte aligned), with a trailer of zero padding, 4 zero bytes and an HMAC-SHA256 at a 16-byte-aligned offset. - [doc] Note ranks: the audio side's event loop keeps, per track, the rank and note that hold it (`0x40fe4c9c + 4t`, `0x40fe4cb4 + 4t`); sequencer notes are rank 1, notes played live rank 2, a note of lower rank is dropped, and a note-off frees the track only with the same rank and note. That is why a held pad or TRIG key pauses the track's own trigs on every stock machine. `[doc]` — `model-cycles-samples#0239456f` [hardware/devices/model-cycles-samples.md:101](https://github.com/70b185/Aggregat/blob/master/hardware/devices/model-cycles-samples.md#L101) · Model:Cycles and Model:Samples - OS 1.13 / Pads, preview notes and the shared sine (model27 notes 60 and 66, MAIN OS 1.13, 2026-11-12)
- [doc] The OS sine `0x8000eee4` (257 Q31 samples in SRAM, copied from the image at boot) is the default wave of every voice operator: the voice reset `0x400a7ab8` (at boot and at each machine change) points all four operators' wave pointers (voice + 168 + 120j) at it. Only KICK (`0x8000eae0` on one operator), METAL (`0x8000f2e8` on two), PERC (`0x4012024c`, in DDR, on one) and CHORD (its own frames) set other waves; SNARE and TONE play only the sine. The waves `0x8000eae0`, the sine and `0x8000f2e8` sit back to back, 1,028 bytes each, after CHORD's last SRAM frame. - [?] [doc] Far tables: the boot hook clears the whole payload, from `0x43000000` to the end of the variables, then copies each image part to its place. So a large read-only table can live in the variables' room, above the code window, and still be filled at boot. model27 puts sections named `.far*` at offset 0 of the package's variables. A far section may hold no relocation of its own.
